purpose: Etodolac is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It can also be used for general pain relief. It helps you feel more comfortable and move more easily day to day.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Etodolac works by blocking the enzymes (called COX-1 and COX-2) that your body uses to make these chemicals. By lowering prostaglandin levels, the medication reduces inflammation and eases your pain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, diarrhea, dizziness, and headache. Some people may notice swelling in their hands or feet. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of heart attack or stroke, especially if taken for a long time or at high doses. It can also cause serious stomach bleeding or ulcers. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Avoid it during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months. Tell your doctor if you have kidney, liver, or heart problems before taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: For arthritis, the usual dose is 300 mg two to three times a day, or 400–500 mg twice a day, depending on what your doctor prescribes. The extended-release tablet is usually taken once a day. Always take the lowest dose that works for you and follow your doctor's instructions closely.
